prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-10-21. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.52 |
| Retained earnings       | 45,920M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,324M |
| Current assets          | 9,606M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 51,071M |
| Total liabilities       | 28,826M |
| Total assets            | 79,897M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,154M |
| Revenue                 | 6,053M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-10-21, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate very strong credit quality, with low leverage (total liabilities/equity of 0.56), solid liquidity (current ratio of 1.52), a substantial equity cushion (64% of assets), massive retained earnings, and healthy EBIT margins (~19%). These factors are consistent with a high-grade profile, though the lack of cash-flow volatility or interest-coverage data prevents an AAA assignment.
DECISION: AA-
